evals.prompt: I want to add a new in-house skill called ecs-service-connect to the APEX skills repo. I have a draft SKILL.md already. Tell me exactly which files I need, which commands to run, and in what order, up to opening the pull request. Step 1 answers: name ecs-service-connect; scope: configuring Amazon ECS Service Connect for service-to-service traffic, for platform engineers; trigger prompts: 'set up ECS Service Connect', 'service discovery between my ECS services', 'Service Connect or Cloud Map', 'route traffic between ECS services without a load balancer', 'troubleshoot Service Connect timeouts'; kind: knowledge; target service: ECS; classes: offer me the ones that fit. You have my yes to the step 1 restate; do not commit, push or open the pull request: list the files, commands and drafts.
expectations: Says to show git ls-files --others skills/ecs-service-connect/ to the contributor, then stage each file by name (for example git add skills/ecs-service-connect/SKILL.md), and says never to use git add -A or git add .
Says to run ./misc/update-all-references.sh and ./misc/update-pages.sh only after the new skill folder is staged, because update-pages.sh lists sources with git ls-files
Says misc/evals/ecs-service-connect/triggering.json is required with at least 16 prompts: at least 8 that should trigger and at least 8 near-miss negatives
Says evals.json needs at least 2 prompts with at least 3 expectations each, the floor check_hygiene.py enforces in CI
Says the SKILL.md front matter must not carry a license field for an in-house skill
Says to ask before pushing a feature branch of the contributor's fork, never pushing to main, and hands the pull request title and body to the contributor to open
Says to add the skill's SKILL_META line to misc/update-pages.sh (folder, page title, a summary under 160 characters and a README group) before running the generators
Offers only classes that have a classes/<name>/class.yaml, names each offered class's parents, and never offers service-eks
Says to draft an ADR under docs/adr/ with Status Proposed, a design-doc note and a fact check section for the pull request body, and asks before drafting a blog

knowledge_assertions.context: Must name the triggering eval file CONTRIBUTING.md requires
Must teach per-file staging after listing untracked files
Must name the SKILL_META line a new skill needs

evals.prompt: My skill eks-node-diagnostics landed in skills/ last month without the eval set CONTRIBUTING.md asks for. Retrofit it: what do I add, how do I update the sibling skills, and how do I get it committed and reviewed? Step 1 answers: name eks-node-diagnostics; scope: diagnosing unhealthy EKS worker nodes, for cluster operators; trigger prompts: 'why is my EKS node NotReady', 'diagnose node pressure on EKS', 'kubelet keeps restarting on my node', 'EKS node failed to join the cluster', 'check node health across my EKS cluster'; kind: discovery; target service: EKS; classes: none for now. You have my yes to the step 1 restate; do not commit, push or open the pull request: list the files, commands and drafts.
expectations: Identifies this as the retrofit mode and does not rewrite the existing SKILL.md unless asked

Says to scaffold misc/evals/eks-node-diagnostics/ (make init-evals SKILL=eks-node-diagnostics, optionally with SIBLINGS=) and fill triggering.json with at least 8 positives and at least 8 near-miss negatives
Says every negative in triggering.json must be attributed in the README SIBLING_MAP block, and each sibling's eval set is updated with update_sibling_map.py in the same pull request
Says to run check_hygiene.py (or make init-evals-finalize SKILL=eks-node-diagnostics) and get exit 0 before opening the pull request
Says to stage by explicit path and to open the pull request from a branch, not push to main

knowledge_assertions.context: Must name the sibling-map block the hygiene check parses
Must name the hygiene check CI runs
Must name the helper that updates each sibling's eval set

evals.prompt: Before I open my PR for a new skill in this repo, which checks should I run locally, and what does each one catch? Step 1 answers: name ecs-task-sizing; scope: right-sizing Amazon ECS task CPU and memory, for platform engineers; trigger prompts: 'size my ECS tasks', 'ECS task CPU and memory limits', 'my ECS tasks run out of memory', 'Fargate task size for my service', 'reduce ECS task cost by right-sizing'; kind: knowledge; target service: ECS; classes: none for now. You have my yes to the step 1 restate; do not commit, push or open the pull request: list the files, commands and drafts.
expectations: Lists python3 misc/validate-frontmatter.py, ./misc/update-all-references.sh --check and ./misc/update-pages.sh --check as the docs-sync checks
Lists python3 misc/evals/scripts/check_hygiene.py as the evals CI check
Says the description is capped at 1024 characters
Says generated files are never hand-edited: the generators are rerun and their output staged by path

knowledge_assertions.context: Must name the front matter validator
Must run the generators in check mode
Must state the description length cap

evals.prompt: I want to add a rule to classes/apex-base/rules.md in the APEX skills repo: every report a skill writes says which skill version produced it. Walk me through everything this change needs before I open the pull request. It adds no new skill. You have my yes to the step 1 restate; do not commit, push or open the pull request: list the files, commands and drafts.
expectations: Identifies this as a class change, not a new skill, and reads classes/steward/class.yaml for the generators to run
Runs or names each Steward generator whose status is exists, and names any `status: planned` generator as not run
Drafts an ADR at docs/adr/NNNN-<slug>.md using the next unused number, with Status Proposed, and adds its row to docs/adr/README.md
Drafts a design-doc note as an edit to docs/design/skill-design.md
Drafts a Fact check section for the pull request body, with a checked on date for each version or service claim, or says the change makes none
Asks the contributor whether they want a blog draft before writing one, and does not write one under misc/website/blog/

knowledge_assertions.context: Must draft the ADR in the ADR folder
A drafted ADR starts as Proposed
